definition.def: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.
examples: They will first send in trained nurses to evaluate the needs of the individual situation. [VERB noun]
The market situation is difficult to evaluate. [VERB noun]

definition.def: the act of forming an opinion of the amount, value or quality of something after thinking about it carefully
examples: an evaluation of the healthcare system
The technique is not widely practised and requires further evaluation.
The discussion includes a critical evaluation of the documentary sources.

examples.sentence: To be at their most effective in their self-regulation, all children can be helped to identify their own ways of learning - metacognition - which will include strategies of planning, monitoring, evaluation, and choice of what to learn.

And to maintain and improve standards, Tourism New Zealand organised a scheme whereby organisations appearing on the website underwent an independent evaluation against a set of agreed national standards of quality.
In Norway, after an intervention campaign was introduced nationally, an evaluation of forty-two schools suggested that, over a two-year period, bullying was halved.
The formal procedures of scientific evaluation provided one framework.
However, the evaluation of some critics has been less enthusiastic.
Now, as well as your own draft report, I've also received some written evaluation from the Association on the work you did during your placement.
